variations.name: Cathode active materials & precursors
variations.description: Producing the lithium-bearing crystal powders (NMC, NCA, LFP/LMFP) and precursor chemicals that store energy on the positive electrode — the single most valuable material in a battery and the key lever on cost, range and critical-mineral dependence.

companies.name: Umicore
companies.what: Belgian materials group making high-nickel NMC CAM and precursors in Europe/Asia with a paused Ontario plant
companies.signal: One of the largest Western CAM makers; cut battery-materials capex ~50% and delayed plants in 2024-25 amid weak EV demand and <40% Western plant utilization

companies.name: BASF
companies.what: Runs the Schwarzheide (Germany) high-nickel CAM plant plus Harjavalta precursors, but has put parts of the battery materials business under review
companies.signal: Schwarzheide began production 2023 targeting ~100 kt/yr; investment scaled back ~50% with facilities delayed in 2024-25

companies.name: EcoPro BM
companies.what: Korea's high-nickel NCA/NCM cathode leader supplying Samsung SDI and SK On, expanding into Canada (with Ford/SK)
companies.signal: Multi-hundred-kt/yr capacity across Korea; KOSDAQ-listed large cap

companies.name: POSCO Future M
companies.what: Korea's only integrated cathode-plus-anode materials maker, vertically tied to POSCO lithium/nickel
companies.signal: GM Ultium CAM JV; tens of kt/yr NCMA capacity ramping

companies.name: Hunan Yuneng
companies.what: World's largest LFP cathode producer, anchor supplier to CATL and BYD
companies.signal: Largest global LFP CAM market share; Shenzhen-listed

companies.name: Nano One Materials
companies.what: Patented one-pot LFP process that skips the wasteful precursor step, run at its Candiac (Québec) plant and offered as licensed technology
companies.signal: Targeting first commercial LFP supply agreements by end-2026; ~$17.8M cash plus $7M raise and $5M NRCan award (late 2025); CEO transition June 2026

companies.name: Mitra Chem
companies.what: AI-accelerated development and US manufacturing of iron-based (LFP/LMFP) cathode materials
companies.signal: ~$96M raised, Series B May 2025; selected for up to $125M in DOE/Michigan awards for a Muskegon plant

companies.name: 6K Energy
companies.what: UniMelt microwave-plasma process making NMC and LFP CAM in seconds without wastewater, replacing multi-day co-precipitation
companies.signal: $50M DOE award executed for the ~$200M+ PlusCAM plant in Jackson, TN (13 kt/yr design)

companies.name: Redwood Materials
companies.what: Planned recycled-content cathode active material in Nevada to feed Panasonic, closing the loop from its recycling business
companies.signal: ~$2B raised incl. $425M Series E (Jan 2026, Google joined); cathode buildout slowed as the company prioritized storage and metals

companies.name: Forge Nano
companies.what: Atomic layer deposition (Atomic Armor) particle coatings that extend cathode powder cycle life and enable higher-nickel chemistries
companies.signal: Venture-backed; coating lines sold to CAM and cell makers, plus its own Forge Battery cell line

variations.name: Anode materials: graphite, synthetic & silicon
variations.description: Making the carbon or silicon powders for the negative electrode — graphite is a mature, China-dominated commodity being onshored for supply security, while silicon-rich anodes promise 20%+ more energy density and faster charging and are just reaching automotive scale.

companies.name: BTR New Material
companies.what: World's largest anode producer across natural and synthetic graphite, supplying most major cell makers
companies.signal: Roughly a quarter of global anode output; expanding to Indonesia/Morocco to skirt trade barriers

companies.name: Novonix
companies.what: First large-scale synthetic graphite production in North America at its Riverside plant in Chattanooga
companies.signal: 20 kt/yr Riverside capacity fully allocated to Panasonic, Stellantis and PowerCo; $754M DOE loan commitment for a second ~31.5 kt/yr plant

companies.name: Vianode
companies.what: Norwegian low-carbon synthetic graphite maker (Herøya) using hydropower-based processing
companies.signal: Announced $3.2B phased St. Thomas, Ontario plant (Nov 2025; production 2028, up to 150 kt/yr) with ~C$670M Ontario loan support

companies.name: Anovion
companies.what: US synthetic graphite pure-play building an $800M facility in Bainbridge, Georgia
companies.signal: ~$117M DOE grant support; 40 kt/yr planned capacity

companies.name: Syrah Resources
companies.what: Vertically integrated natural graphite — Balama mine (Mozambique) feeding the Vidalia, Louisiana active anode material plant
companies.signal: Balama shut ~1 year by protests triggering DFC/DOE loan defaults; $98M DOE loan now under forbearance to 2027 and Tesla offtake dispute resolved; ~$291M total debt

companies.name: Sila
companies.what: Titan Silicon nano-composite silicon anode powder as a drop-in graphite replacement
companies.signal: >$1.3B raised; automotive-scale Moses Lake, WA plant started production 2025; Mercedes-Benz and Panasonic deals

companies.name: Group14 Technologies
companies.what: SCC55 silicon-carbon anode material made in scaled silane-to-powder factories
companies.signal: $463M round (Aug 2025) led by SK with Porsche, ATL, Microsoft; three factories operating across US and Korea

companies.name: NanoGraf
companies.what: Silicon-oxide anode materials powering US military cells, with EV-grade Onyx material next
companies.signal: Hundreds of thousands of defense cells in 2025; Michigan plant targeted online 2027

companies.name: Nexeon
companies.what: UK-developed silicon anode material produced in Gunsan, Korea, co-located with OCI for fenceline silane supply
companies.signal: First volume plant delivering from 2025 under a binding Panasonic supply agreement

companies.name: OneD Battery Sciences
companies.what: SINANODE silicon nanowires fused onto graphite — shut down after EV demand softened
companies.signal: Shuttered its Moses Lake pilot plant and ceased operations (2024-25) despite GM backing — evidence of silicon-anode shakeout

variations.name: Electrolytes, separators & inactive cell components
variations.description: Supplying the ion-carrying liquid electrolyte, the microporous separator film between electrodes, and inactive parts like foils, binders and current collectors — low-glamour commodities that gate cell safety, cost and the localization of battery supply chains.

companies.name: Asahi Kasei
companies.what: World-leading separator maker (Hipore wet-process plus Celgard dry-process subsidiary); building a C$1.8B separator plant in Port Colborne, Ontario with Honda
companies.signal: Multi-billion-m2/yr capacity; Canada plant announced 2024 for ~2027 production

companies.name: SEMCORP (Yunnan Enjie)
companies.what: World's largest wet-process separator producer, expanding from China into Hungary and the US
companies.signal: Dominant global separator share; supplies CATL, LG, Samsung

companies.name: SK IE Technology
companies.what: Korean premium ceramic-coated separator maker with plants in Korea and Poland
companies.signal: KRX-listed; capacity rationalized in 2024-25 amid EV slowdown

companies.name: ENTEK
companies.what: The only US-owned lithium-ion separator manufacturer, building a wet-process plant in Terre Haute, Indiana
companies.signal: Up to $1.2B DOE loan with first $77M disbursement approved (2025); ~$1.7B total project

companies.name: Tinci Materials
companies.what: World's largest electrolyte producer with backward integration into LiPF6 and LiFSI salts
companies.signal: Leading global electrolyte share; Shenzhen-listed; building European capacity

companies.name: Enchem
companies.what: Korean electrolyte maker that followed SK and Ultium to the US with Georgia and Tennessee plants
companies.signal: KOSDAQ-listed; among first localized US electrolyte suppliers

companies.name: Soulbrain
companies.what: Korean specialty chemicals group supplying electrolytes and high-purity process chemicals, with US production for auto cell plants
companies.signal: Long-standing supplier to Samsung SDI/LG; US subsidiaries operating

companies.name: South 8 Technologies
companies.what: Liquefied gas (LiGas) electrolyte that keeps cells working to -60°C and vents inertly for safety
companies.signal: Venture-backed San Diego startup; defense and cold-climate cell programs

companies.name: Soteria Battery Innovation Group
companies.what: Metallized-film current collectors and ceramic separator architecture that stop internal-short fires, licensed through an industry consortium
companies.signal: 100+ member licensing consortium including major materials and cell makers

variations.white_space: Asian incumbents control ~90% of separator and electrolyte capacity at brutal commodity cost points, so almost no startups attack the category head-on; the opening is policy-driven localization (ENTEK is the lone US-owned separator maker) and step-change chemistries like liquefied-gas or solid electrolytes rather than cost competition.

variations.name: EV powertrain: motors, e-axles, inverters & SiC power electronics
variations.description: The hardware that turns battery energy into motion — electric motors, integrated e-axles, inverters and silicon-carbide power semiconductors — where efficiency gains directly buy range and cost reduction per vehicle.

companies.name: BorgWarner
companies.what: Full e-propulsion portfolio: integrated drive modules, 800V SiC inverters and motors for global OEMs
companies.signal: Multi-billion-dollar ePropulsion segment shipping at volume

companies.name: ZF Friedrichshafen
companies.what: E-axles and electric drive systems for cars and commercial vehicles; restructuring its E-division amid slower EV ramp
companies.signal: Millions of e-drive units delivered; announced major cost restructuring 2024-25

companies.name: Nidec
companies.what: Largest merchant e-axle supplier (E-Axle) in the China/Japan market, fighting a bruising price war
companies.signal: Took losses on EV traction business and restructured, incl. reworked Stellantis JV

companies.name: YASA
companies.what: Axial-flux motors with ~4x power density of radial machines, powering Mercedes-AMG, Ferrari and Lamborghini hybrids; now developing an in-wheel motor
companies.signal: Mercedes-Benz subsidiary since 2021; opened UK axial-flux 'super factory' in 2025 scaling beyond 25,000 motors/yr

companies.name: DeepDrive
companies.what: Munich dual-rotor radial-flux motor claimed to cut magnet/iron use and cost ~20%, offered as central drive and in-wheel unit
companies.signal: €30M Series B (Sep 2024, Leitmotif + BMW i Ventures); co-development with 8 of the 10 largest OEMs

companies.name: Equipmake
companies.what: UK spoke-architecture motors, inverters and electrification kits for buses, aerospace and specialty vehicles
companies.signal: FY25 results show severe financial difficulty — net assets fell to £0.3M after losses, impairment and restructuring, despite new contracts (JCB, Textron)

companies.name: Niron Magnetics
companies.what: Iron-nitride permanent magnets with zero rare earths, aimed at EV traction motors exposed to China's rare-earth export controls
companies.signal: GM/Stellantis-backed; Plant 1 in Sartell, MN under construction (operations early 2027) with $10M state grant; site hunt for $1.8B full-scale plant

companies.name: Wolfspeed
companies.what: Vertically integrated silicon-carbide wafers and devices (200mm Mohawk Valley fab) for EV inverters
companies.signal: Emerged from Chapter 11 on Sep 29, 2025 with ~70% less debt and ~$926M liquidity after SiC demand undershot

companies.name: Infineon
companies.what: World's #1 power semiconductor maker; SiC and IGBT modules for most EV inverter platforms, with the Kulim SiC mega-fab
companies.signal: Multi-billion-euro automotive power semi revenue; SiC capacity ramping

companies.name: Vitesco Technologies
companies.what: EV inverters, e-axles and power electronics spun off from Continental
companies.signal: Acquired by Schaeffler — merger completed October 2024, forming a top-tier e-mobility supplier

variations.name: Packs, modules, enclosures & thermal management (cell-to-pack, immersion cooling)
variations.description: Engineering how cells are structured, protected and kept at temperature — cell-to-pack/cell-to-body integration cuts weight and cost, while thermal barriers and immersion cooling prevent fires and enable extreme fast charging.

companies.name: CATL
companies.what: Pioneer of cell-to-pack integration; third-gen Qilin pack reaches ~72% volume utilization without modules
companies.signal: World's largest battery maker; CTP deployed across hundreds of GWh

companies.name: BYD
companies.what: Blade LFP cell-to-body architecture where long cells are structural pack members
companies.signal: Blade packs in millions of vehicles; licensed/supplied to Tesla, Toyota

companies.name: XING Mobility
companies.what: Taiwanese immersion-cooled battery packs where cells sit in dielectric fluid, sold for EVs, ESS and AI data-center backup power
companies.signal: TotalEnergies MOU (July 2025) on immersion fluids; debuted 800V immersion-cooled BBU at Supercomputing 2025 and CES 2026

companies.name: Carrar
companies.what: Israeli two-phase immersion-cooled modules claiming passive containment of thermal runaway even with a cell above 800°C
companies.signal: $5.3M Series A with strategic investor Gentherm; moving to commercial module production

companies.name: Aspen Aerogels
companies.what: PyroThin aerogel cell-to-cell thermal barriers that stop runaway propagation, designed into GM and Toyota EV packs
companies.signal: NYSE-listed; energy industrial + EV thermal barrier revenue in the hundreds of millions

companies.name: Constellium
companies.what: Aluminum battery enclosures and crash-management structures for high-volume EV platforms
companies.signal: Supplies major EU/US OEM battery programs from automotive structures plants

companies.name: Our Next Energy (ONE)
companies.what: Michigan LFP pack maker (Aries) with a Gemini dual-chemistry range-extender architecture
companies.signal: Raised ~$300M Series B (2023) then hit a funding crunch with layoffs and CEO change; operations continue at reduced scale

variations.white_space: Cold plates are good enough for mainstream passenger EVs, so immersion cooling has few players despite better physics; the opening is fast-charge heavy-duty trucks, defense vehicles and AI data-center backup units where extreme duty cycles justify the fluid's cost and weight — exactly where XING and Carrar are pivoting.

variations.name: BMS & battery health analytics software
variations.description: Software that estimates battery state, predicts degradation and optimizes charging/dispatch from onboard controllers or the cloud — squeezing more life, safety and revenue out of every installed kWh in EVs and grid storage.

companies.name: TWAICE
companies.what: Munich battery analytics platform for grid storage and EV fleets covering performance, warranty and safety monitoring
companies.signal: ~$75M raised plus €24M EIB venture debt (2025); analytics across large BESS fleets

companies.name: ACCURE Battery Intelligence
companies.what: Aachen-based predictive analytics that flags cell anomalies before fires across storage, bus and marine fleets
companies.signal: $34.5M raised; Series B closed Feb 2025; multi-GWh monitored

companies.name: Zitara
companies.what: Embedded plus cloud battery state-estimation software used by operators from grid storage to satellites
companies.signal: $29M raised; acquired by Fortescue's Elysia in January 2026 — early consolidation signal

companies.name: Elysia (Fortescue)
companies.what: Battery intelligence platform born from Williams Advanced Engineering, combining onboard controls with cloud analytics; bought Zitara to deepen the stack
companies.signal: Backed by Fortescue's balance sheet; Zitara acquisition closed Jan 2026

companies.name: Breathe Battery Technologies
companies.what: Physics-based adaptive charging and battery models embedded into BMS firmware for Volvo and consumer-electronics OEMs
companies.signal: $21M Series B (May 2025) led by Kinnevik with Lowercarbon and Volvo Cars Tech Fund

companies.name: Eatron Technologies
companies.what: Automotive-grade AI BMS software stack (edge + cloud) licensed to OEMs and cell makers
companies.signal: Raised new growth funding; partnerships for AI-powered battery health on mainstream silicon

companies.name: Qnovo
companies.what: Adaptive charging algorithms that extend cycle life, long deployed in smartphones and moving into EVs
companies.signal: Long-running adaptive-charging pioneer licensing to consumer and automotive OEMs

companies.name: Analog Devices
companies.what: Precision battery-monitoring ICs and the wireless BMS chipset used in GM's Ultium packs
companies.signal: Dominant share in battery monitoring silicon

variations.name: Battery manufacturing equipment & dry-electrode processing
variations.description: The machines that mix, coat, calender, stack and form cells — a sector dominated by Chinese full-line suppliers, with solvent-free dry-electrode coating emerging as the disruptive process that deletes giant drying ovens and slashes plant energy and capex.

companies.name: Wuxi Lead Intelligent
companies.what: World's largest battery manufacturing equipment supplier, delivering full turnkey cell production lines to CATL, Tesla and European gigafactories
companies.signal: Dominant global market share in Li-ion production tools

companies.name: Dürr
companies.what: German plant engineering group supplying electrode coating and solvent-recovery lines (with Techno Smart)
companies.signal: Active battery coating equipment orders in EU/US

companies.name: Bühler
companies.what: Continuous electrode slurry mixing systems that replace batch mixers at gigafactory scale
companies.signal: Continuous mixers deployed at multiple gigafactories

companies.name: Manz AG
companies.what: German battery cell production equipment maker that collapsed when European gigafactory orders evaporated
companies.signal: Filed insolvency Dec 2024; proceedings opened Feb 2025; Reutlingen site sold to Tesla Automation, remaining business wound down

companies.name: AM Batteries
companies.what: Electrostatic powder-to-electrode spray that deposits dry active material directly onto foil, cutting coating energy ~40%
companies.signal: TIME Best Inventions recognition; roll-to-roll pilot lines with cell-maker partners

companies.name: LiCAP Technologies
companies.what: Activated Dry Electrode process producing free-standing electrode films under heat and pressure, claiming up to 50% cost reduction
companies.signal: 300 MWh dry-coating line commissioned in Sacramento; scaling with European equipment partners

companies.name: Anaphite
companies.what: Bristol (UK) dry-coating process IP designed to retrofit into existing gigafactory lines, now focused on LFP
companies.signal: >$15M raised incl. £1.4M/€1.6M top-up (Dec 2025) for LFP dry-coating development

companies.name: Matthews International
companies.what: Owns key dry-electrode calendering equipment and IP (supplied Tesla's 4680 dry process; litigated over trade secrets)
companies.signal: Energy division equipment shipped to multiple dry-electrode programs

variations.white_space: Manz's insolvency shows Western toolmakers cannot beat Wuxi Lead and peers on cost or speed for conventional wet lines; the credible wedge is dry-electrode processing, which resets the capex stack (no NMP solvent ovens or recovery) and is still young enough that no equipment incumbent owns the standard.

variations.name: Hydrometallurgical & pyrometallurgical recycling
variations.description: Shredding end-of-life batteries and production scrap into black mass and then recovering lithium, nickel and cobalt with acid leaching (hydromet) or smelting (pyromet) — the backbone of battery circularity, currently long on shredding capacity and short on profitable refining.

companies.name: Redwood Materials
companies.what: Largest North American recycler integrating collection, black mass and refined nickel/lithium products at its Nevada and South Carolina campuses
companies.signal: ~$2B raised; $425M Series E closed Jan 2026 (Google joined); ~$200M revenue; turned down its DOE loan

companies.name: Ascend Elements
companies.what: Hydro-to-Cathode process turning black mass directly into pCAM/CAM at Apex 1 in Kentucky
companies.signal: $542M Series D (2023); delayed Kentucky CAM line after an offtaker pulled out and lost a $164M DOE grant (a $316M grant remains)

companies.name: Li-Cycle
companies.what: Spoke-and-hub hydromet model whose Rochester hub cost ballooned from $560M toward $1B and never ran
companies.signal: Filed for bankruptcy May 2025; Glencore (its secured lender) bought the assets for ~$40M, completed Aug 8, 2025

companies.name: Cirba Solutions
companies.what: US battery materials processor (EQT/Marubeni-backed) running multiple plants and building lithium-ion capacity in Ohio and South Carolina
companies.signal: Lancaster, OH output up ~600% since 2022 on ~$82M DOE grants; $200M DOE grant for Columbia, SC intact

companies.name: Glencore
companies.what: Feeds batteries and black mass into its Sudbury nickel smelter and now owns the former Li-Cycle spoke network
companies.signal: Completed Li-Cycle takeover Aug 2025, adding NA/EU recycling footprint

companies.name: Brunp (CATL)
companies.what: World's largest battery recycler, closing the loop into CATL's own cathode supply in China
companies.signal: 100kt+/yr class processing capacity; majority-owned by CATL

companies.name: Umicore
companies.what: Pyro+hydro refining of battery and precious metals at Hoboken, Belgium, with recycled-content CAM offerings
companies.signal: Decades of metals refining; battery recycling expansion slowed with the EU market

companies.name: Hydrovolt
companies.what: Norway's large-scale pack shredding/black-mass producer (Hydro JV), which opened Europe's first industrial-scale hydromet plant in June 2025
companies.signal: ~10,000 t/yr hydromet capacity; survived co-parent Northvolt's collapse (Northvolt's own Revolt hub closed)

companies.name: cylib
companies.what: Aachen spinout with end-to-end water-based recycling recovering lithium and graphite as well as metals
companies.signal: €55M Series A; building a €180M+ Dormagen plant billed as Europe's largest, with ~$30M EU grant (Sep 2025)

companies.name: tozero
companies.what: Munich startup recovering lithium and graphite from black mass, scaling from pilot toward industrial output
companies.signal: Venture-backed; transitioning pilot processes to industrial scale in Germany

companies.name: Altilium
companies.what: UK EcoCathode hydromet recovering lithium, nickel and graphite, building the UK's first commercial-scale recycling plant with integrated refining (Plymouth ACT3, Teesside planned)
companies.signal: SQM-backed; ACT3 under construction with EV OEM sample agreements

companies.name: Eramet
companies.what: French miner that designed a Dunkirk battery-recycling hydromet plant, then suspended it for lack of European feedstock and pCAM customers
companies.signal: Dunkirk project suspended (late 2024) — emblematic of Europe's recycling overcapacity vs. weak downstream demand

variations.name: Direct & cathode-to-cathode recycling
variations.description: Regenerating cathode powder while preserving its engineered crystal structure (plasma, relithiation or direct precursor synthesis) instead of dissolving everything to metal salts — promising far lower cost and emissions, but only if feedstock chemistry is known and still in demand.

companies.name: Princeton NuEnergy
companies.what: Low-temperature plasma-assisted (LPAS) purification that regenerates NMC and LFP cathode directly from spent cells
companies.signal: >$55M raised (Honda, Samsung, Shell Ventures, LKQ); Chester, SC flagship — the first US commercial-scale direct-recycling/CAM plant — fully commissioned Aug 2025, expanding to 15 kt/yr in 2026

companies.name: Ascend Elements
companies.what: Hydro-to-Cathode direct precursor synthesis that skips separating black mass into individual metal salts
companies.signal: Process running at Covington, GA base plant; Kentucky CAM expansion delayed

companies.name: Green Li-ion
companies.what: Modular GLMC units converting black mass straight into battery-grade pCAM/cathode rather than metal salts
companies.signal: First US plant in Atoka, Oklahoma started 2024 at ~2 t pCAM/day with plans to quadruple

companies.name: OnTo Technology
companies.what: Oregon pioneer of 'cathode healing' direct recycling, licensing IP rather than building plants
companies.signal: Long-running R&D/licensing shop; current commercial traction unclear

companies.name: Aqua Metals
companies.what: Electrochemical Li AquaRefining that plates metals back out of black mass with electricity instead of chemical reagents
companies.signal: Nasdaq micro-cap; pilot ran 24/7 for over a year producing >99.5% lithium carbonate and signed a supply agreement with 6K Energy, but capital constraints stalled its Sierra ARC campus

variations.white_space: Direct recycling stays thin because it needs clean, single-chemistry feedstock and the regenerated cathode must still match market demand — recovered NMC risks obsolescence as the fleet shifts to LFP. The opening is LFP and manufacturing scrap: metal values there are too low for hydromet to pencil, so structure-preserving regeneration is the only route that creates value, which is why PNE's LFP-capable SC plant matters.

variations.name: Second-life EV battery stationary storage
variations.description: Repurposing retired EV packs — which typically retain 75-80% capacity — into stationary storage at roughly half the cost of new batteries, deferring recycling while supplying cheap grid and commercial power capacity.

companies.name: B2U Storage Solutions
companies.what: Pack-level plug-and-play architecture using unmodified EV packs in cabinet enclosures for utility-scale solar+storage
companies.signal: Multiple operating CA sites plus Texas expansion; launched a 7-project structured finance fund and a battery supply deal with Waymo (2025)

companies.name: Moment Energy
companies.what: UL-certified commercial-scale second-life BESS manufactured at its Vancouver hub with OEM supply deals (Mercedes-Benz, Nissan)
companies.signal: $40M Series B (May 2026), >$100M total raised; full-scale production reached 2025; DOE award toward a US gigafactory

companies.name: Redwood Energy (Redwood Materials)
companies.what: Repurposes inbound EV packs into microgrids before recycling them, including the 12MW/63MWh Crusoe AI-data-center microgrid in Nevada
companies.signal: Launched 2025 with the world's largest second-life deployment; GWh-scale pack pipeline from Redwood's collection network

companies.name: Element Energy
companies.what: Cell-level adaptive BMS that safely mixes heterogeneous used cells, enabling the 53 MWh Texas plant — the largest second-life grid system
companies.signal: 53 MWh ERCOT system commissioned Nov 2024 with LG Energy Solution Vertech partnership targeting 2 GWh

companies.name: Connected Energy
companies.what: UK E-STOR containerized systems built on Renault and Forsee Power packs for C&I sites
companies.signal: Backed by Caterpillar, Volvo Energy and M&G; positioning for the late-2020s EV retirement wave

companies.name: Voltfang
companies.what: Aachen-based maker of C&I storage from requalified European automotive battery modules
companies.signal: €15M Series B (June 2025); opened 'Europe's largest second-life battery factory' scalable to 1 GWh/yr, targeting +250 MWh deployed by end-2026

companies.name: Octave
companies.what: Brussels startup pairing second-life (and LFP) cabinets with its own energy-management software for SMEs and industrial sites
companies.signal: 100+ battery cabinets sold, >13 MWh of packs given a second life; seed-funded (SPDG, Périer-D'Ieteren)

companies.name: Smartville
companies.what: Containerized MOAB storage built from validated second-life packs across mixed OEMs, made in California
companies.signal: $5.9M DOE award; commercial deployments with utility partners

companies.name: 4R Energy (Nissan/Sumitomo)
companies.what: The original second-life venture, refabricating Nissan Leaf packs for storage and replacement batteries in Japan since 2010
companies.signal: Operating Namie plant; longest-running second-life program

companies.name: Mercedes-Benz Energy
companies.what: Builds grid-scale storage in Germany from retired and spare-part EV packs and supplies packs to partners like Moment Energy
companies.signal: Multiple MW-scale German second-life plants since 2016
